question: Should OpenClaw expose Discord bot presence mutation to plugins as a public runtime API, and what gate, account scoping, and precedence model should it use?
rationale: The source already has internal presence mutation paths, but promoting one to `api.runtime.channel.discord` changes the public plugin contract and gives plugin code a bot-credential-backed control plane.

options.title: Design a gated runtime API
options.body: Add a narrow Discord-owned `updatePresence`-style runtime seam with explicit action/config gating, account selection, docs, tests, and precedence against static config, auto-presence, and `setPresence`.

options.title: Keep message action only
options.body: Leave dynamic presence mutation on the existing default-off `setPresence` message action and document that plugins should not mutate Discord presence directly.

options.title: Fold into self-profile design
options.body: Defer this behind https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/34004 if maintainers want one Discord identity/profile API instead of a separate presence-only plugin API.

recommendation.title: Design a gated runtime API
recommendation.body: Add a narrow Discord-owned `updatePresence`-style runtime seam with explicit action/config gating, account selection, docs, tests, and precedence against static config, auto-presence, and `setPresence`.

likelyOwner.reason: The unresolved choice is primarily a public plugin-runtime seam and security-boundary decision, and this owner has the strongest runtime-boundary history signal in the inspected files.
